E068-01.notes: Original is a comma splice (two independent clauses). C is a fused sentence; D 'and, their' misplaces the comma after the conjunction. B is the only acceptable option. The semicolon fix is not offered, so B is the only correct choice.

E068-02.notes: B is redundant and informal ('a lot of very many'); C is wordy and ungrammatical, with 'numerous' left dangling; D is redundant ('many thousands ... in large numbers'). Fact: the builders planted hundreds of thousands of trees and shrubs, so 'many thousands of trees' is accurate.

E068-03.notes: The sentence contrasts natural appearance with deliberate design, which needs a concessive word. Because and Since make a causal claim that is illogical, and Unless gives a nonsensical condition.

E068-04.notes: B produces 'below for crosstown traffic below the level', which says 'below' twice and is garbled. C 'tucked also roads' has awkward word order. D 'tucked, for crosstown traffic, roads below' can be parsed, but it is awkward and splits the verb from its object, so it is clearly worse than A. Fact: the sunken transverse roads were part of the Greensward Plan, so this is accurate.

E068-05.notes: The added sentence gives new information (the name 'transverse roads' and that the roads are still used), so B's claim that it repeats sentence 5 is false. A misdescribes the sentence, which says nothing about traffic laws. D is unsupported. Adding a fact about present-day use is a slight drift, but it fits naturally after sentence 5. Fact: the 65th/66th, 79th, 86th, and 97th Street transverses still carry crosstown traffic, so the claim is accurate.

E068-06.notes: The sentence needs a plain plural subject for 'owned'. A and B are possessives with nothing to possess. C is singular and does not fit 'more than half of the'. Fact: Central Park Conservancy and NYC sources report that over half of Seneca Village's African American households owned property (per the 1855 census), so the claim is accurate. Also checked: about 225 residents in 1855 and roughly two-thirds African American, with Irish and German residents making up the rest; both are accurate.

E068-07.notes: No comma belongs between a compound subject and its verb. C places the comma after 'and'; D places commas wrongly in two spots. Fact: Seneca Village had three churches and a school (Colored School No. 3), and its buildings were razed after residents were removed around 1857, so the claim is accurate.

E068-08.notes: 'Today' calls for the simple present. B, C, and D clash with 'Today'. Fact: Central Park gets roughly 40 million visits a year, so 'millions' is accurate and understated.

E068-09.notes: Only A refers to Seneca Village and the overlooked cost. B and D give present-day facts but say nothing about the cost; C is about Olmsted and is off-topic. Fact: since about 2000, historians, an archaeological excavation in 2011, and Conservancy signage and exhibits have worked to commemorate Seneca Village, so the claim is accurate. D's '800+ acres' (843 acres) is also accurate.

E068-10.notes: The essay covers design in about one paragraph and then turns to Seneca Village. A is false because no tree-by-tree detail is given. C is false because the roads get only one sentence. D is false because sentence 4 says the park was designed.
